fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench
  harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench) run under supervision,
  plus manual `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` for debugging — NO
  scheduled-or-gate live runs in the PR path. A proven flake (red in ≥2
  distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h) is quarantined via
  `scripts/test_quarantine.json` (checked in, reviewed in the fix PR;
  `flake-watch.yml` files the issue and opens the PR) — the gate legs pipe
  their targets through `scripts/apply_quarantine.py`, while nightly
  KEEPS running the file to produce the un-quarantine repeat-run proof.
  Flake intake consumes PR-dispatch runs only (gh-1537:
  `scripts/flake_watch.py` filters to `workflow_dispatch` events — the
  retired main trigger leaves SM validation dispatches and v* tag runs;
  a red tag run is a release-flow failure, triaged by daily-publish /
  ci-red-report, never quarantined as a flake). Dedup is per test name
  (the #1364 lesson): one test red across N runs files ONE issue.
- `cd flutter_app && flutter test --exclude-tags integration` green
  (includes golden suite; integration-tagged `test/cli_visual` runs
  pre-merge in ci.yml's `pty-visual` leg — gh-1538 retired the nightly
  duplicate — and on demand).

content.text:
build-extension:
    name: Build Chrome extension
    needs: version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily cli watcher's budget arithmetic (#351).
    timeout-minutes: 30
    if: inputs.create_release == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: write
      # gh-2026: defense-in-depth for the release_tag_mint.sh
      # train-verification probe (`gh run list` on the tag ref); the
      # probe itself authenticates with RELEASE_PAT (gh prefers
      # GH_TOKEN, which every mint-reachable call site exports), so
      # this grant matters only if the probe is ever switched to the
      # job token. Granted on every mint-reachable job.
      actions: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Blobless full history: the lazy draft create (gh-1801 rework)
          # builds the release body via scripts/release_notes.sh — same
          # reason as release-macos's checkout (gh-1477).
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          # gh-1684 decision 4 (gate symmetry): the SAME exact patch pin
          # the pages.yml leg carried and the PR gate carries (#1431 —
          # the rev normalization absorbs canvaskit rev-hash churn, the
          # pin keeps every fa-extension.zip build comparable across
          # legs). The old unpinned `channel: stable` floated the engine
          # per run — one of the two ways the release and Pages legs
          # diverged.
          flutter-version: '3.47.7'
          channel: stable

      - name: dart pub get (root)
        run: dart pub get

      # browser_ext/dart is a separate package (path dep on this root), so
      # its pub get must follow the root's — same as browser-ext.yml.
      - name: dart pub get (browser_ext/dart)
        run: cd browser_ext/dart && dart pub get

      # Full artifact: SW agent (dart2js) + the Flutter panel app embedded,
      # exactly what "Load unpacked" expects. --clobber keeps the stable
      # asset name fa-extension.zip pointing at the newest build (the
      # landing page links it directly).
      - name: Build extension zip
        run: bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh --with-app

      # AC1 (#1096): per-entry uncompressed size table + +5% budget gate
      # against the committed baseline (gh-2004: reseeded to the post-gemma
      # vendored-engines shape — transformers/webllm are intentional CWS
      # policy; growth beyond the floor fails the release).
      # Identical invocation as the PR-time gate (ci.yml
      # extension-size-gate): one baseline, one enforcement rule.
      - name: Size manifest + budget gate (fa-extension.zip)
        run: python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/fa-extension.zip --baseline scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv

      - name: Upload extension to the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          asset="fa-extension.zip"
          cp build/fa-extension.zip "$asset"
          ls -lh "$asset"

          # gh-1801 (rework): DRAFT-first, NEVER publish here. The
          # extension zip is not a `fa update` asset — and even a CLI
          # asset alone would not make the release servable: the SIGNED
          # SHA256SUMS only lands in the tag-run's release-provenance job,
          # which owns the --draft=false --latest flip. Create the draft
          # with the curated notes + the draft-owner marker (so the guard
          # step below can reclaim it on failure) and upload.
          bash scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh "$RELEASE_TAG"
          # gh-2042 AC1: the immutability gate owns the attach — a
          # PUBLISHED release (the same-tag convergence race) skips
          # attached assets and refuses unattached fa-* assets loud
          # instead of silently drifting the signed SHA256SUMS.
          bash scripts/release_asset_gate.sh "$RELEASE_TAG" "$asset"

      # Draft lifecycle invariant (issue #282): this job creates releases,
      # so a failed/cancelled run must not leave one behind as a draft.
      - name: Draft lifecycle guard (delete orphaned draft on failure)
        if: always() && job.status != 'success'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
        run: bash scripts/release_draft_guard.sh "$RELEASE_TAG"

  release-macos:
    name: Create macOS GitHub Release
    needs: [version, build-macos]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily cli watcher's budget arithmetic (#351).
    timeout-minutes: 15
    if: inputs.create_release == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: write
      # gh-2026: defense-in-depth for the release_tag_mint.sh
      # train-verification probe (`gh run list` on the tag ref); the probe
      # itself authenticates with RELEASE_PAT (gh prefers GH_TOKEN, which
      # every mint-reachable call site exports), so this grant matters
      # only if the probe is ever switched to the job token.
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Full history: release_notes.sh falls back to "commits since the
          # previous tag" when the CHANGELOG has no section for this version.
          # gh-1477: blobless — the notes read commit MESSAGES, never
          # historical file blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0

💡 **SUGGESTION: pair the hosted CLI lane's pre-warm with the `hooks-shared-` cache restore — the established ci.yml / build-mobile.yml hosted-lane pattern**

This lane runs on fresh GitHub-hosted workspaces (`macos-latest` / `macos-15-intel`), so every release train re-downloads both dylibs live from upstream. The pre-warm's bounded retries fix the gh-2075 failure class — but the repo's pinned hosted-lane pattern (`test/ci_sqlite3_hook_prewarm_guard_test.dart` AC2/AC6) is **cache restore + pre-warm**, which additionally makes warm runs skip the network entirely:

```yaml
- name: Native-assets hook cache
  uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
  with:
    path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
    key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
    restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
```

placed immediately before this step (after checkout, so `hashFiles('pubspec.lock')` resolves the committed lockfile). On a warm cache the tool reports `0 fetched, 1 already verified` with zero egress, and a brownout window then cannot touch the leg at all — strictly closer to the "network-independent build" goal the PR description states. Optionally mirror the ci.yml hardening (`timeout-minutes: 2`, `continue-on-error: true`) so a cache-service hiccup can never red the leg.

The self-hosted app-build lane needs nothing extra — its persistent workdir already carries `.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared` across runs.
